findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (RCS H-801), vote 62 to 47
findings.note: Voted aye on the House concurring in the Senate changes to HB 958. The ratified bill requires a voter registration application to affirmatively state US citizenship before it is processed (a blank answer gets a notice and 30 days to return a statement under penalty of perjury), bars staff from proceeding with an application that does not affirm citizenship, and sets up state-board removal of voters flagged as possible non-citizens from a federal database. It also adds monthly motor-vehicle data sharing and cross-state list checks. It does not add a photo ID rule. The Governor vetoed it on 2026-08-17.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (RCS H-758), vote 66 to 47
findings.note: Voted aye on second reading of HB 958 in the House. The edition then before the House (edition 6) already contained the citizenship-on-registration provisions. Same date: aye on amendment A2 (Blackwell, RCS H-756, 69 to 44) and aye on amendment A1 (Blackwell, RCS H-755); no on amendment A3 (Dahle, RCS H-757, failed 47 to 66). The content of these amendments was not read.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes: bill history, Governor's veto 2026-08-17; override calendar 2026-09-02
findings.note: Bill page shows the primary sponsors are Blackwell and Stevens and the cosponsors are Blust, Dixon, Kidwell, Penny, Pike and Ward. Charles W. Miller is not listed as a sponsor. The bill was ratified 2026-08-06, vetoed 2026-08-17, and last placed on the calendar for 2026-09-02. No override vote by Miller appears on his votes page.

findings.motion: HB 958 ratified text, Part II sections 2.3 and 2.4 (reference for what the votes above covered)
findings.note: Section 2.4 adds G.S. 163-83: the county board processes a voter registration application only if it affirmatively indicates the applicant is a citizen of the United States. Section 2.3(b) requires a State Board process to remove voters flagged as potential non-citizens by a federal database. Effective January 1, 2027.
